title: Add requirements map doc with correct line citations, plus changelog ent
summary: Retry of a job that creates docs/design/requirements-map.md (mapping BRIEF.md requirements to evidence) and a CHANGELOG.md entry. The last attempt failed on wrong CHANGELOG line citations (off by four after the entry was added), a mis-ranged S5 citation, and a missing BRIEF.md:102 'Restarting' row; fix all three.

defaults_applied.how: Every claim in the map cites file and line, checked against the final tree.
Doc written for an outside reader.
One doc plus one changelog entry.
Recovered intent from the prior verification findings.
Citations are checked against the final tree by the verifier.

assumptions: The original request (074419-sczw) is not visible; I infer the deliverable from the failed verification: docs/design/requirements-map.md plus a 4-line CHANGELOG.md entry near the top.
The file does not exist in the current tree, so it is created from scratch.
Line citations refer to files in the final (post-change) tree, as the doc's section 1 states.

acceptance_criteria.text: docs/design/requirements-map.md exists and states that line numbers refer to files in the same tree.
Every CHANGELOG.md line citation in the map matches the final CHANGELOG.md, including the '## [0.1.0]' heading and 'The speedup is not measured.' after the new entry is added.
The S5 citation points to the exact lines of the bullet it describes (the crate bullet containing 'eight evidence rules that no waiver clears').
BRIEF.md:102 ('Restarting: ...') has its own row in the map, not only indirect coverage.
Every other BRIEF.md citation in the map matches the quoted text at that line.
CHANGELOG.md has a new entry for the map and no other changes.
Run `git diff` and `git status`: only docs/design/requirements-map.md and CHANGELOG.md changed; no governance files touched.
Run `cargo fmt --check`, `cargo clippy`, and `cargo test`: all pass unchanged.

departures: Slightly lower p_reading_accepted because the original request text is not visible and the file is inferred; citation accuracy is a repeated failure mode, so pass probability is not raised.
